statement.p: A differentiable function f(x,y) has the property that f(1,2)=5 and f_x(1,2)=6 and f_y(1,2)=-4. Find the equation of the tangent plane at the point on the surface z=f(x,y) where x=1, y=2.

static.solution: (1,2,5) lies on the surface. The surface is the level surface of the function F(x,y,z) = f(x,y) - z = 0 . The normal to the surface at the point (1,2,5) is \nabla F(1,2,5) = f_x(1,2)\vec i + f_y(1,2)\vec j - \vec k= 6 \vec i - 4 \vec j - \vec k. Thus the equation of the tangent plane is 6 x - 4 y - z = 6 (1) - 4 (2) - 5 or z = 5+6\mathopen{}\left(x-1\right)+\left(-4\right)\mathopen{}\left(y-2\right).
